prompt: Split a string into words using a regex: any run of non-letter characters is a separator, and empty strings never appear in the result. Complete the split method in WordSplitter.
explanation: String.split takes a regular expression, and the character class [^A-Za-z] matches any character that is NOT an ASCII letter; adding + makes a whole run of separators count as one split point. split can still produce an empty first element when the string starts with a separator, so the results are filtered before being copied into the returned array.
hints: Inside [ ], a leading ^ negates the class: [^A-Za-z] matches any non-letter.
Append + so that a run like ";;" or "  " acts as a single separator: s.split("[^A-Za-z]+").
A leading separator leaves an empty string at index 0. Collect non-empty parts into an ArrayList and finish with toArray(new String[0]).
